public.title: Clone Graph
public.description: adjacency serializes a connected undirected graph: row i lists the 1-based labels adjacent to node i+1. It has 0 to 50 nodes, no repeated edges or self-loops, and neighbor order is significant. First clone the graph. Then each edit [node,label] appends label to that node’s neighbor row in the clone only, in edit order. Edits are intentionally directed, may repeat labels or add self-loops, and have valid labels from 1 through the row count. There are at most 100 edits; an empty graph has none. Return {original,clone}: original must retain the input adjacency values and clone must reflect the edits. Preserve existing neighbor order. This JSON observation makes row independence testable through clone-only mutations.
hints: Copy every neighbor row, not only the outer array.
Apply each edit to the cloned row while retaining the original adjacency structure.
public.attribution: Original statement, examples, tests and solutions authored for Bekor, 2026, for a standard algorithmic problem. No third-party exercise text or solution code used.

javascript.signature: cloneGraph(adjacency: number[][], edits: number[][]): { original: number[][]; clone: number[][] }

typescript.signature: cloneGraph(adjacency: number[][], edits: number[][]): { original: number[][]; clone: number[][] }

explanation: Copy every adjacency row to obtain independent neighbor arrays, then append each edit to the clone. Returning both structures makes aliasing failures visible as changed original values. O(V+E+edits) time and space.
